svg.title: Model-built navigation serves a time-bounded review
svg.desc: Place model-built navigation beneath the oversized corpus and six-day clock. Tooling enables pointing into evidence; it is not another source of incident facts.

**Location:** `metr-review-workspace`

**Frame:** The left column, in the register [page 075](075.md) used. The six-day clock. The
transcripts that run past the panel edge. Beneath them, something [page 077](077.md) never drew: the
navigation tooling itself, built by a model so that the corpus could be pointed at.

**Screen / system text — INVESTIGATOR, 4 SEPTEMBER 2026 (PARAPHRASED):**
`WE USED A MODEL TO BUILD TOOLS THAT WOULD POINT US AT THE SMALL PARTS WORTH READING.`

`THE TOOL COULD NOT READ A WHOLE TRANSCRIPT EITHER. IT DIVIDED THEM AMONG OTHER AGENTS.`

**Action:** The instrument that made the record navigable was itself made by the instrument.

**Provenance:** `documented` — `HF-POD`, attributed paraphrase of Ajeya Cotra describing her
own investigation. Chapter 5 has shown models reading the corpus since [page 076](076.md); this is the
layer beneath that, and the book had not drawn it.

", "title": "Model-built navigation serves a time-bounded review" } }
